successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: Latium Vetus: the Alban hills, Tusculum, Aricia, Lanuvium, Lavinium, Ardea, Tibur and Praeneste, without Rome's own land

ledger.x: 672 BC: Alba Longa, the league's head, 'completely destroyed' by Tullus Hostilius (672-640), its population moved to Rome (year = start of the reign).
496-493 BC: 'Rome defeated the Lavinii and the Tusculi in the battle of Lake Regillus, 496 BC'; 'Roman tradition links the Foedus Cassianum to a Roman victory at Lake Regillus'.

493 BC: the Foedus Cassianum, 'Rome allied with the league in 493 BC'; shares of loot and Roman generals 'in command of joint campaigns'; 'unclear whether Rome joined the league or signed as a separate party'.
340-338 BC: the Latin War ('341/340- 338 BC'): Vesuvius (340), Trifanum (339), Pedum and the Astura (338).
338 BC: 'The defeated Latin peoples were obliged to recognize Roman suzerainty'; towns Romanized, given Roman magistracies or made colonies.
338 BC: 'Disestablished: 338 BC'; 'Following the Roman victory, the league was dissolved'; Rome 'renamed the cities municipia, established coloniae within them'.

certainty.note: Thirty small city-states in the Alban hills and the coast south of the Tiber; the land is a circle around the hills less Rome's own.
